label: NPS (RADIUS)
description: Network Policy Server (NPS) is the Microsoft implementation of a Remote Authentication Dial-In User Service (RADIUS) server and proxy. NPS enables centralized authentication, authorization, and accounting (AAA) for network access scenarios including 802.1X wired/wireless authentication, VPN connections (SSTP, IKEv2, L2TP), and dial-up connections. NPS uses Active Directory for user account validation and supports multiple EAP authentication methods including EAP-TLS (certificate-based), PEAP-MSCHAPv2 (username/password), and PEAP-TLS. NPS enforces network access policies through Connection Request Policies (CRPs) and Network Policies (NPs), allowing fine-grained control over network access based on user groups, device types, time restrictions, and other conditions.

l1: What Windows Server version is the NPS server running on? (Get-ComputerInfo | Select WindowsProductName, WindowsVersion, OsBuild)
Is the Network Policy Server service (IAS) running and set to Automatic? (Get-Service IAS | Select Name,Status,StartType,DisplayName)
What authentication scenario is this — 802.1x wired, 802.1x wireless, SSTP/IKEv2 VPN, L2TP VPN, or RADIUS proxy authentication?
What is the exact symptom — authentication rejected, no RADIUS response (timeout at NAS), NPS service not responding, or wrong VLAN/attribute assigned?
Is this affecting all users/devices, specific user accounts, specific device types, or a specific RADIUS client (NAS)?
What RADIUS client (NAS) is involved — network switch, wireless access point, or VPN concentrator? What is the NAS device IP address? (netsh nps show client)
Is the RADIUS shared secret configured identically on both NPS and the NAS device — including case sensitivity and special characters?
When did the issue start — NPS certificate renewal, Group Policy change, AD group change, NPS server upgrade, or NAS firmware update?

Are there NPS authentication failure events in the Windows Security event log? (Get-WinEvent -LogName Security -FilterXPath "*[System[(EventID=6273)]]" | Select TimeCreated,Message | Select -First 10)

Is Windows Firewall allowing RADIUS traffic on UDP ports 1812 (authentication) and 1813 (accounting)? (Get-NetFirewallRule | Where DisplayName -like "*RADIUS*" | Select DisplayName,Enabled,Direction,Action)
l2: What EAP method is configured in the NPS Network Policy — EAP-TLS (certificate-based machine or user auth), PEAP-MSCHAPv2 (username/password), or PEAP-TLS? (netsh nps show np)
Is NPS acting as a standalone RADIUS server, or is it configured as a RADIUS Proxy forwarding requests to a Remote RADIUS Server Group? (netsh nps show config)
Which Connection Request Policy (CRP) and Network Policy (NP) are matching the failing authentication requests — what are their conditions and order? (netsh nps show crp; netsh nps show np)

Is the NPS server computer account a member of 'RAS and IAS Servers' security group in AD (required to read user dial-in properties)? (Get-ADGroupMember -Identity "RAS and IAS Servers" | Select Name,SamAccountName)

Is the NPS server TLS certificate trusted by authenticating clients — is the full CA certificate chain present and the root CA certificate distributed to clients via GPO? (Get-ChildItem Cert:\LocalMachine\My | Where Subject -like "*<NPS FQDN>*" | Select Subject,Thumbprint,NotAfter,Issuer)

Is the authenticating AD account enabled, not locked out, not expired, and does it have the correct dial-in permission? (Get-ADUser <username> -Properties Enabled,LockedOut,PasswordExpired,AccountExpirationDate,msNPAllowDialin | Select *)

Is RADIUS Accounting configured and working — are accounting Start/Stop/Interim packets from the NAS reaching NPS on UDP 1813? (Get-NetUDPEndpoint -OwningProcess (Get-Process -Name IAS).Id | Where LocalPort -eq 1813)
For RADIUS Proxy: are realm routing rules correctly mapping domain suffixes to the correct Remote RADIUS Server Group? (netsh nps show remoteserver)
Is the NPS IAS log configured and capturing full authentication detail records? (Get-Item C:\Windows\System32\LogFiles\IN*.log | Select Name,Length,LastWriteTime)
Are there multiple NPS servers for redundancy — is the NAS device configured with both primary and secondary NPS servers? (netsh nps show client)
What is the NPS database configuration — using local SQL or remote SQL for logging? (netsh nps show config)
Are there any NPS templates configured — Shared Secrets, RADIUS Clients, or Network Policies? (netsh nps show template)
Is the NPS server experiencing high CPU or memory utilization during authentication attempts? (Get-Process -Name IAS | Select CPU,WorkingSet,PM)
Are there any recent Windows updates installed that might affect NPS functionality? (Get-HotFix | Sort InstalledOn -Descending | Select -First 5)

l1: On the NPS server: open Security event log — filter for Event ID 6273 — share the Reason Code (field 9), Reason description, and User-Name. (Get-WinEvent -LogName Security -FilterXPath "*[System[(EventID=6273)]]" | Select TimeCreated,Message | Format-List)
Run 'Get-Service IAS | Select Name,Status,StartType,DisplayName' — verify the NPS service is running and configured for automatic startup.
Run 'netsh nps show client' — confirm the NAS device IP is listed as a RADIUS client with the correct shared secret. (netsh nps show client > C:\nps_clients.txt)
Is the user's AD account enabled and not locked? 'Get-ADUser <username> -Properties Enabled,LockedOut,BadLogonCount,AccountExpirationDate,msNPAllowDialin | Select *'
What error does the end client/device display — 'Authentication failed', 'Certificate is not valid', 'Server certificate not trusted', or 'Username/password incorrect'?

Review the NPS IAS log: C:\Windows\System32\LogFiles\IN<date>.log — find the record for the failing User-Name and note the Reason-Code and NAS-IP-Address. (Get-Content C:\Windows\System32\LogFiles\IN*.log | Select-String '<username>')
Test RADIUS reachability from the NAS: use 'Test-NetConnection -ComputerName <NPS_IP> -Port 1812' or 'portqry -n <NPS IP> -e 1812 -p udp' from the NAS device.
Check Windows Firewall for RADIUS rules: 'Get-NetFirewallRule | Where DisplayName -like "*RADIUS*" | Select DisplayName,Enabled,Direction,Action,Profile'
Verify NPS is listening on RADIUS ports: 'Get-NetUDPEndpoint -OwningProcess (Get-Process -Name IAS).Id | Select LocalPort,OwningProcess'
Check for recent NPS service crashes in System event log: 'Get-WinEvent -LogName System -FilterXPath "*[System[(EventID=7031 or EventID=7034)]]" | Select TimeCreated,Message'
l2:
Enable NPS verbose trace: 'netsh nps set tracing mode=all' — reproduce the failure — disable: 'netsh nps set tracing mode=none' — share C:\Windows	racing
ps.log. (Copy-Item C:\Windows	racing
ps.log C:
ps_trace.log)
Run 'netsh nps show np' — list all Network Policies, their order, enabled/disabled state, and conditions. (netsh nps show np > C:\nps_network_policies.txt)
Run 'netsh nps show crp' — list all Connection Request Policies, conditions, and RADIUS server groups. (netsh nps show crp > C:\nps_crp_policies.txt)

Verify the NPS server TLS certificate: 'Get-ChildItem Cert:\LocalMachine\My | Where Subject -like "*<NPS FQDN>*" | Select Subject,Thumbprint,NotAfter,Issuer,EnhancedKeyUsageList,SubjectAlternativeNames'
Verify the CA root cert is in Trusted Root CAs on clients: 'Get-ChildItem Cert:\LocalMachine\Root | Where Subject -like "*<CA name>*" | Select Subject,Thumbprint,NotAfter'
Verify NPS server is in 'RAS and IAS Servers' group: 'Get-ADGroupMember -Identity "RAS and IAS Servers" | Where Name -eq "<NPS server name>"'
Check CRL accessibility for NPS server cert: 'certutil -verify -urlfetch C:\nps_server.cer' — does CRL/OCSP check pass? Export cert first: 'certutil -store My <NPS FQDN> C:\nps_server.cer'

Capture RADIUS packet trace: 'netsh trace start capture=yes IPv4.Address=<NPS_IP> UDP.Port=1812 tracefile=C:\nps_radius.etl' — reproduce — 'netsh trace stop' — analyze with Message Analyzer or Wireshark.
Check user dial-in attribute: 'Get-ADUser <user> -Properties msNPAllowDialin | Select msNPAllowDialin' — $null = NPS policy controls; $false = always denied regardless of policy.

For RADIUS proxy: 'netsh nps show remoteserver' — confirm remote RADIUS server IPs and shared secrets; test reachability from NPS proxy to backend NPS on UDP 1812. (Test-NetConnection -ComputerName <backend_NPS_IP> -Port 1812)
Check NPS registry configuration: 'Get-ItemProperty "HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\IAS\Parameters" | Select *'
Verify EAP configuration in registry: 'Get-ItemProperty "HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\IAS\Parameters\Profiles" | Select *'
Test AD connectivity from NPS: 'Test-ADDSForestHealth -Identity <forest_name>' or 'Get-ADDomainController -Filter * | Select Name,IPv4Address,OperatingSystem'
Check for NPS database issues: 'Get-ItemProperty "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\IAS\Parameters" | Select SqlDatabaseConnectionString,SqlLogFileName'
Verify the NPS server's SPN is registered: 'setspn -Q IAS/<NPS_FQDN>' and 'setspn -Q TERMSRV/<NPS_FQDN>'
Check for certificate auto-enrollment issues: 'certutil -pulse' and review Certificate Services client logs in Application event log.

l1: NPS Event 6273 Reason Codes reference: 0=no error, 16=auth method not supported/mismatch, 22=user account not found, 23=password incorrect, 48=no NPS policy matched request, 65=EAP negotiation failure, 66=account locked, 67=account expired, 68=account disabled, 69=password expired, 70=dial-in denied.

Verify RADIUS shared secret is byte-for-byte identical on NPS and the NAS — even a trailing space causes all authentications to fail with RADIUS Message-Authenticator mismatch. Use PowerShell to compare: (netsh nps show client | Select-String <NAS_IP>)
Unlock and confirm AD account: 'Unlock-ADAccount -Identity <user>; Get-ADUser <user> -Properties LockedOut,Enabled,PasswordExpired | Select LockedOut,Enabled,PasswordExpired'

Verify the NPS Network Policy conditions exactly match the request attributes — check NAS-Port-Type, NAS-IP-Address, Windows Groups, and HCAP conditions. Use 'netsh nps show np' to review policy order and conditions.

Restart NPS service: 'Restart-Service IAS -Force' — verify Event ID 4400 (NPS started) appears in System log within 30 seconds. (Get-WinEvent -LogName System -FilterXPath "*[System[(EventID=4400)]]" | Select -First 1)

Confirm UDP 1812 reachability from NAS to NPS — check Windows Firewall rule: 'Get-NetFirewallRule | Where DisplayName -like "*RADIUS*" | Select DisplayName,Enabled,Direction,Action,Profile' — ensure rules are enabled for correct profiles (Domain/Private/Public).
For authentication timeouts: increase RADIUS timeout on NAS device to minimum 30 seconds for EAP-TLS (requires 3-8 round trips) and 15 seconds for PEAP-MSCHAPv2.
Verify NPS service startup type: 'Set-Service IAS -StartupType Automatic' — ensure service starts automatically after server reboot.
Check for port conflicts: 'Get-NetUDPEndpoint | Where LocalPort -in @(1812,1813)' — ensure no other processes are using RADIUS ports.
Review NPS event log for service startup errors: 'Get-WinEvent -LogName System -Source IAS -MaxEvents 50 | Select TimeCreated,Id,LevelDisplayName,Message'
l2: For EAP-TLS failure: verify the client cert has Client Authentication EKU (OID 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.2), is not expired, has correct SAN/CN matching the user principal name, and is issued by a CA that NPS trusts in its Trusted Root CAs store. (certutil -store My <cert_thumbprint>)

For EAP-TLS: verify the NPS server certificate has Server Authentication EKU (OID 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.1), the subject matches the NPS FQDN, and the certificate chain is complete. (Get-ChildItem Cert:\LocalMachine\My | Where Subject -like "*<NPS_FQDN>*" | Select *)

For PEAP-MSCHAPv2 failure with incorrect credentials: verify the RADIUS NAS is sending the correct User-Name format (domain\user or user@domain) and that the account exists in that domain. Check NPS IAS log for User-Name field.

For PEAP-MSCHAPv2: ensure the 'Validate server certificate' option is disabled on clients if using self-signed certificates, or ensure the NPS server certificate is trusted by clients via GPO or manual installation.

For no policy match (Reason 48): check Connection Request Policy first — if the CRP condition does not match, NPS does not even evaluate Network Policies. Review NAS-Port-Type, Called-Station-Id, and Client-IPv4-Address conditions in the CRP. Use 'netsh nps show crp' to review.

For RADIUS proxy misrouting: 'netsh nps show remoteserver' — confirm realm suffix routing rules; ensure the RADIUS proxy can resolve and reach backend NPS IPs on UDP 1812. (Test-NetConnection -ComputerName <backend_NPS> -Port 1812)

For expired NPS certificate: re-enroll via 'certlm.msc > Personal > Request new certificate' — then update EAP properties in NPS console (Network Policy > Constraints > Authentication > EAP Types > Edit > Select new certificate).

For msNPAllowDialin = $false: either set to $null (policy-controlled) — 'Set-ADUser <user> -Clear msNPAllowDialin' — or set to $true for explicit allow — 'Set-ADUser <user> -Replace @{msNPAllowDialin=$true}'.

For certificate revocation check failure: if CRL is offline, NPS will reject EAP-TLS by default — temporarily disable revocation checking for testing only in NPS console (Network Policy > Constraints > Authentication > EAP Types > Edit > Validate Server Certificate > Uncheck).

For RADIUS accounting failures: verify UDP 1813 is open on NPS firewall — 'Get-NetFirewallRule | Where LocalPort -eq 1813' — ensure accounting is enabled on the NAS device and the NAS IP is configured as a RADIUS client in NPS.
For RADIUS timeout at the NAS: increase RADIUS server timeout on the NAS device — EAP-TLS requires 3-8 round trips — set timeout to minimum 30 seconds, PEAP-MSCHAPv2 to 15 seconds.

Analyze the NPS verbose trace (nps.log) — look for 'IAS_AUTH_FAILED', 'IAS_CORRUPT_DATA', 'IAS_NO_RECORD', 'EAP_TYPE_NOT_SUPPORTED', or 'CERT_CHAIN_ERROR' entries correlated with the failing user/device. (Get-Content C:\Windows\tracing\nps.log | Select-String <username>)

For 802.1X authentication issues: verify the switch/AP is configured with the correct EAP type, authentication mode (port-based or MAC-based), and RADIUS server settings. Check switch logs for EAPOL exchange failures.

For VPN authentication issues: verify the VPN server (RRAS) is configured with the correct RADIUS server IP, shared secret, and authentication type. Check RRAS event log for RADIUS communication errors.

For machine authentication vs user authentication: ensure NPS Network Policy conditions distinguish between machine auth (using machine certificate) and user auth (using user certificate or credentials). Use 'Condition > Windows Groups' or 'Condition > NAS-Port-Type' to differentiate.

For VLAN assignment issues: verify the NPS Network Policy has the correct 'Tunnel-Pvt-Group-ID' (RADIUS attribute 81) configured for the target VLAN. Check switch configuration for VLAN assignments from RADIUS.

For time-restricted access failures: verify the NPS Network Policy 'Day and Time Restrictions' condition matches the current time of the authentication attempt. Check NPS server and client time synchronization.

For NPS database logging issues: if using SQL logging, verify the SQL server is reachable, the database exists, and the connection string in registry is correct. Test with 'Test-NetConnection -ComputerName <SQL_server> -Port 1433'.

For NPS high availability issues: verify NPS is configured in an NPS NLB cluster or with multiple NPS servers. Check that the NAS device has all NPS server IPs configured as RADIUS clients with shared secrets.

For AD replication delays: if using multi-domain forests, verify the NPS server can contact domain controllers for the user's domain. Use 'Get-ADDomainController -Discover -DomainName <user_domain>' to verify DC discovery.

For smart card authentication failures: verify the smart card reader is functional, the smart card certificate is valid and has Client Authentication EKU, and the user PIN is correct. Check event log for smart card errors.

For health policy (NAP) failures: verify the SHA (System Health Agent) is installed and configured on clients, the SHV (System Health Validator) is configured on NPS, and the health policy conditions match the client's compliance state.

Enable NPS verbose trace: 'netsh nps set tracing mode=all' — reproduce the failure — disable: 'netsh nps set tracing mode=none' — collect C:\Windows	racing
ps.log with 'Copy-Item C:\Windows	racing
ps.log C:
ps_trace.log'
Run 'netsh nps show crp > C:\nps_connection_request_policies.txt' — exports all Connection Request Policies with conditions and server groups.

Run 'Get-ChildItem Cert:\LocalMachine\My | Select Subject,Thumbprint,NotAfter,Issuer,EnhancedKeyUsageList,SubjectAlternativeNames | Out-File C:\nps_certificates.txt' — collects all certificates in the Personal store.

Collect AD domain controller information: 'Get-ADDomainController -Filter * | Select Name,IPv4Address,OperatingSystem,Site,Enabled | Out-File C:\nps_domain_controllers.txt'
Collect recent hotfixes: 'Get-HotFix | Sort InstalledOn -Descending | Select HotFixID,InstalledOn,Description | Out-File C:\nps_hotfixes.txt'
Collect process information: 'Get-Process -Name IAS | Select Name,CPU,WorkingSet,PM,Id,HandleCount,Threads | Out-File C:\nps_process_info.txt'

TSS full data collection: '.\TSS.ps1 -Scenario NET_NPS' — run on the NPS server, reproduce the authentication failure, stop when prompted. This collects comprehensive diagnostics including registry, event logs, configuration, and traces.

Collect NPS SQL logging configuration: 'Get-ItemProperty "HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\IAS\Parameters" | Select SqlDatabaseConnectionString,SqlLogFileName,SqlLogFrequency | Out-File C:\nps_sql_config.txt' if SQL logging is configured.
Collect SPN information: 'setspn -Q IAS/* > C:\nps_spn_ias.txt' and 'setspn -Q TERMSRV/* > C:\nps_spn_termsrv.txt' — verifies NPS service principal names.

auth_rejected_reason_code.title: Authentication rejected — NPS Event 6273
auth_rejected_reason_code.description: This playbook addresses NPS authentication failures indicated by Event ID 6273 in the Security event log. The Reason Code field in the event message is critical for determining the root cause. Common reason codes include: 16 (authentication method not supported), 22 (user account not found), 23 (incorrect password), 48 (no NPS policy matched), 65 (EAP negotiation failure), 66 (account locked), 67 (account expired), 68 (account disabled), 69 (password expired), and 70 (dial-in denied). The playbook systematically verifies NPS service status, AD account state, RADIUS client configuration, and Network Policy matching to isolate and resolve the authentication failure.

phases.name: Verify
phases.description: Verify NPS service is running and identify the authentication failure reason code from the Security event log.

steps.action: Get-Service IAS | Select Name,Status,StartType,DisplayName
steps.expect: Status: Running, StartType: Automatic

steps.action: Get-WinEvent -LogName Security -FilterXPath "*[System[(EventID=6273)]]" | Select -First 5 | Format-List TimeCreated,Message
steps.expect: Note Reason Code field (field 9) — this drives the entire investigation

steps.action: Reason Code reference: 16=EAP method mismatch, 22=account not found, 23=wrong password, 48=no policy matched, 65=EAP negotiation failed, 66=account locked, 67=account expired, 68=account disabled, 69=password expired, 70=dial-in denied
steps.expect: Match reason code to root cause category

phases.name: Isolate
phases.description: Isolate the root cause by checking AD account state, RADIUS client configuration, and Network Policy matching.

steps.action: Get-ADUser <username> -Properties Enabled,LockedOut,PasswordExpired,AccountExpirationDate,msNPAllowDialin | Select *
steps.expect: Account enabled, not locked, password not expired, msNPAllowDialin not set to $false

steps.action: netsh nps show client
steps.expect: NAS device IP listed with correct shared secret — trailing space in secret causes all auths to fail

steps.action: netsh nps show np
steps.expect: Network policies listed in correct order — first matching policy wins; verify policy conditions match request attributes

steps.action: netsh nps show crp
steps.expect: Connection Request Policies listed in correct order — CRP must match before Network Policies are evaluated

phases.name: Fix
phases.description: Apply fixes based on the identified root cause: unlock accounts, correct shared secrets, or adjust policy conditions.

steps.action: Unlock-ADAccount -Identity <user> (if Reason 23 and account locked)
steps.expect: Account unlocked — retry authentication

steps.action: Verify and re-enter RADIUS shared secret on both NPS and NAS device (if Reason 16 or auth fails silently)
steps.expect: Secrets match byte-for-byte including case and special characters — use PowerShell to compare

steps.action: Reorder or fix NPS Network Policy conditions to match the request attributes (if Reason 48)
steps.expect: Policy now matches — check NAS-Port-Type, Windows Groups, and NAS-IP-Address conditions

steps.action: Set-ADUser <user> -Clear msNPAllowDialin (if msNPAllowDialin=$false)
steps.expect: Dial-in permission cleared to allow NPS policy control

steps.action: Reset user password and force change at next logon (if Reason 23 or 69)
steps.expect: Password reset — user must authenticate with new password

phases.name: Confirm
phases.description: Verify the fix by checking for successful authentication events in the Security log.

steps.action: Get-WinEvent -LogName Security -FilterXPath "*[System[(EventID=6272)]]" | Select -First 3 | Format-List TimeCreated,Message
steps.expect: Event 6272 = authentication succeeded — confirms fix worked

steps.action: Test authentication from affected client device or NAS
steps.expect: Authentication succeeds without errors

eap_tls_cert_failure.title: EAP-TLS certificate authentication failing
eap_tls_cert_failure.description: This playbook addresses EAP-TLS authentication failures, which use client and server certificates for mutual authentication. Common causes include expired or invalid certificates, missing CA certificates in the Trusted Root store, certificate revocation list (CRL) unavailability, incorrect Enhanced Key Usage (EKU) extensions, and subject name mismatches. EAP-TLS is commonly used for 802.1X wired/wireless authentication and VPN connections requiring certificate-based authentication. The playbook verifies certificate validity, chain trust, CRL accessibility, and NPS EAP configuration.

phases.name: Verify
phases.description: Verify the NPS server certificate and identify EAP-TLS failure events in the Security log.

steps.action: Get-WinEvent -LogName Security -FilterXPath "*[System[(EventID=6273)]]" | Select -First 3 | Format-List TimeCreated,Message
steps.expect: Reason Code 65 = EAP negotiation failed; note the full reason description

steps.action: Get-ChildItem Cert:\LocalMachine\My | Where Subject -like '*<NPS FQDN>*' | Select Subject,Thumbprint,NotAfter,Issuer,EnhancedKeyUsageList,SubjectAlternativeNames
steps.expect: NPS server cert present, not expired, has Server Authentication EKU (OID 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.1)

phases.name: Isolate
phases.description: Isolate the certificate chain issue by checking CRL accessibility, CA trust, and client certificate validity.

steps.action: certutil -store My <NPS_FQDN> C:\nps_server.cer; certutil -verify -urlfetch C:\nps_server.cer
steps.expect: CRL and OCSP checks pass — if CRL unreachable, NPS rejects EAP-TLS by default

steps.action: Get-ChildItem Cert:\LocalMachine\Root | Where Subject -like '*<CA name>*' | Select Subject,Thumbprint,NotAfter
steps.expect: Issuing CA root cert in Trusted Root CAs on NPS server

steps.action: On client: certutil -store My — check client cert Subject, NotAfter, EKU, and SAN
steps.expect: Client cert has Client Authentication EKU (OID 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.2), not expired, correct SAN or CN matching user principal name

steps.action: On client: Get-ChildItem Cert:\LocalMachine\Root | Where Subject -like '*<CA name>*'
steps.expect: Issuing CA root cert in Trusted Root CAs on client device

phases.name: Fix
phases.description: Fix certificate issues by renewing expired certificates, distributing CA certificates, or configuring CRL settings.

steps.action: Re-enroll NPS server cert via certlm.msc > Personal > Request new certificate (if expired)
steps.expect: New cert enrolled — update EAP type in NPS Network Policy to select new certificate

steps.action: Push CA root cert to clients via GPO: Computer Config > Windows Settings > Security Settings > Public Key Policies > Trusted Root CAs
steps.expect: Clients now trust the NPS server certificate chain

steps.action: Configure CRL distribution points to be accessible from NPS server and clients
steps.expect: CRL checks pass — NPS accepts certificates with valid revocation status

steps.action: Temporarily disable revocation checking for testing: NPS console > Network Policy > Constraints > Authentication > EAP Types > Edit > Validate Server Certificate > Uncheck
steps.expect: EAP-TLS succeeds with revocation checking disabled — use only for troubleshooting

phases.name: Confirm
phases.description: Verify EAP-TLS authentication succeeds after certificate fixes.

steps.action: Get-WinEvent -LogName Security -FilterXPath "*[System[(EventID=6272)]]" | Select -First 3 | Format-List TimeCreated,Message
steps.expect: Event 6272 = authentication succeeded with EAP-TLS

steps.action: Test authentication from affected client device
steps.expect: EAP-TLS authentication succeeds without certificate errors

peap_mschapv2_failure.title: PEAP-MSCHAPv2 authentication failing
peap_mschapv2_failure.description: This playbook addresses PEAP-MSCHAPv2 authentication failures, which use username/password credentials with TLS-protected channel. Common causes include incorrect username format (domain\user vs user@domain), incorrect passwords, account lockouts, NPS server certificate trust issues on clients, password expiration, and dial-in permission misconfigurations. PEAP-MSCHAPv2 is commonly used for 802.1X authentication where certificate deployment to all clients is not feasible. The playbook verifies credentials, account state, certificate trust, and NPS configuration.

phases.name: Verify
phases.description: Verify NPS service and identify PEAP-MSCHAPv2 failure events with specific reason codes.

steps.action: Get-WinEvent -LogName Security -FilterXPath "*[System[(EventID=6273)]]" | Select -First 5 | Format-List TimeCreated,Message
steps.expect: Reason Code 23 (incorrect password), 22 (account not found), or 65 (EAP negotiation failed)

steps.action: Get-ChildItem Cert:\LocalMachine\My | Where Subject -like '*<NPS FQDN>*' | Select Subject,NotAfter,Issuer
steps.expect: NPS server cert present and valid

phases.name: Isolate
phases.description: Isolate the credential or certificate trust issue by checking AD account state and client certificate trust.

steps.action: Get-ADUser <username> -Properties Enabled,LockedOut,PasswordExpired,AccountExpirationDate,msNPAllowDialin | Select *
steps.expect: Account enabled, not locked, password not expired

steps.action: Review NPS IAS log: Get-Content C:\Windows\System32\LogFiles\IN*.log | Select-String '<username>'
steps.expect: Check User-Name format sent by NAS — should be domain\user or user@domain

steps.action: On client: verify NPS server certificate is in Trusted Root CAs
steps.expect: Client trusts NPS server certificate or 'Validate server certificate' is disabled in client PEAP settings

steps.action: Test authentication with known good credentials
steps.expect: If good credentials work, issue is with the specific user account or password

phases.name: Fix
phases.description: Fix credential or certificate trust issues by resetting passwords, unlocking accounts, or distributing certificates.

steps.action: Unlock-ADAccount -Identity <user> (if account locked)
steps.expect: Account unlocked — retry authentication

steps.action: Reset user password: Set-ADAccountPassword -Identity <user> -Reset -NewPassword (ConvertTo-SecureString -AsPlainText '<new_password>' -Force)
steps.expect: Password reset — user authenticates with new password

steps.action: Configure NAS to send correct User-Name format (domain\user or user@domain)
steps.expect: NPS receives correct username format and can locate the AD account

steps.action: Push NPS server CA certificate to clients via GPO if 'Validate server certificate' is enabled
steps.expect: Clients trust NPS server certificate chain

steps.action: Disable 'Validate server certificate' on clients if using self-signed NPS certificate (not recommended for production)
steps.expect: Clients accept NPS server certificate without validation

phases.name: Confirm
phases.description: Verify PEAP-MSCHAPv2 authentication succeeds after fixes.

steps.action: Get-WinEvent -LogName Security -FilterXPath "*[System[(EventID=6272)]]" | Select -First 3 | Format-List TimeCreated,Message
steps.expect: Event 6272 = authentication succeeded with PEAP-MSCHAPv2

steps.action: Test authentication from affected client device
steps.expect: PEAP-MSCHAPv2 authentication succeeds

radius_proxy_misrouting.title: RADIUS proxy misrouting to backend servers
radius_proxy_misrouting.description: This playbook addresses RADIUS proxy configuration issues where authentication requests are not being correctly forwarded to backend RADIUS servers. Common causes include incorrect realm suffix routing rules, unreachable backend NPS servers, mismatched shared secrets between proxy and backend, and incorrect Connection Request Policy configuration. RADIUS proxy is used in multi-forest environments or when NPS servers are deployed in different network segments. The playbook verifies proxy configuration, backend server connectivity, and routing rules.

phases.name: Verify
phases.description: Verify RADIUS proxy configuration and identify routing failures.

steps.action: netsh nps show config
steps.expect: NPS configured as RADIUS proxy with Remote RADIUS Server Groups defined

steps.action: netsh nps show remoteserver
steps.expect: Backend RADIUS server IPs and shared secrets are configured

steps.action: Get-WinEvent -LogName Security -FilterXPath "*[System[(EventID=6273)]]" | Select -First 5 | Format-List TimeCreated,Message
steps.expect: Reason Code indicates proxy communication failure or no policy matched

phases.name: Isolate
phases.description: Isolate the routing issue by checking backend server connectivity and realm routing rules.

steps.action: Test-NetConnection -ComputerName <backend_NPS_IP> -Port 1812
steps.expect: TCP/UDP connectivity to backend NPS on port 1812 succeeds

steps.action: netsh nps show crp
steps.expect: Connection Request Policy with realm suffix conditions is configured and enabled

steps.action: Review NPS IAS log for proxy forwarding attempts
steps.expect: Log shows which backend server the request was forwarded to and the response

steps.action: Verify shared secret matches between proxy and backend NPS
steps.expect: Shared secrets are identical on both proxy and backend server

phases.name: Fix
phases.description: Fix routing issues by correcting realm rules, ensuring connectivity, or updating shared secrets.

steps.action: Add or correct realm suffix routing rule in Connection Request Policy
steps.expect: Requests with matching realm suffix are routed to correct backend server group

steps.action: Configure firewall rules to allow UDP 1812/1813 between proxy and backend NPS
steps.expect: Network connectivity established between proxy and backend servers

steps.action: Update shared secret on both proxy and backend NPS to match exactly
steps.expect: Shared secrets match — proxy can authenticate to backend NPS

steps.action: Configure DNS resolution for backend NPS FQDNs if using FQDN in remote server configuration
steps.expect: Proxy can resolve backend NPS hostnames

phases.name: Confirm
phases.description: Verify RADIUS proxy correctly forwards requests to backend servers.

steps.action: Get-WinEvent -LogName Security -FilterXPath "*[System[(EventID=6272)]]" | Select -First 3 | Format-List TimeCreated,Message
steps.expect: Event 6272 = authentication succeeded via proxy

steps.action: Review NPS IAS log for successful proxy forwarding
steps.expect: Log shows request forwarded to backend and Access-Accept received

steps.action: Test authentication from client through proxy to backend
steps.expect: Authentication succeeds through proxy

network_policy_match_failure.title: No Network Policy matched (Reason Code 48)
network_policy_match_failure.description: This playbook addresses authentication failures where no Network Policy matches the request (Reason Code 48). This occurs when Network Policy conditions do not match the attributes sent by the NAS, or when policies are disabled or in the wrong order. Common causes include incorrect NAS-Port-Type conditions, Windows Group mismatches, IP address condition errors, and disabled policies. Connection Request Policies are evaluated first, so CRP issues can also cause Reason 48. The playbook verifies policy order, conditions, and matching attributes.

phases.name: Verify
phases.description: Verify NPS policy configuration and identify Reason Code 48 events.

steps.action: Get-WinEvent -LogName Security -FilterXPath "*[System[(EventID=6273)]]" | Select -First 5 | Format-List TimeCreated,Message
steps.expect: Reason Code 48 = no NPS policy matched request

steps.action: netsh nps show crp
steps.expect: Connection Request Policies are configured and enabled

steps.action: netsh nps show np
steps.expect: Network Policies are configured, enabled, and in correct order

phases.name: Isolate
phases.description: Isolate the policy mismatch by comparing request attributes to policy conditions.

steps.action: Review NPS IAS log: Get-Content C:\Windows\System32\LogFiles\IN*.log | Select-String '<username>'
steps.expect: Log shows NAS-Port-Type, NAS-IP-Address, Called-Station-Id, and other request attributes

steps.action: Compare request attributes to Connection Request Policy conditions
steps.expect: At least one CRP condition must match for Network Policies to be evaluated

steps.action: Compare request attributes to Network Policy conditions
steps.expect: At least one NP condition must match for the policy to apply

steps.action: Check if policies are disabled or have 'Grant Access' vs 'Deny Access' settings
steps.expect: Policies are enabled and configured to grant access

phases.name: Fix
phases.description: Fix policy conditions by adjusting matching criteria or reordering policies.

steps.action: Enable disabled Connection Request Policy or Network Policy
steps.expect: Policy is now evaluated during authentication

steps.action: Adjust NAS-Port-Type condition to match the actual NAS type (Ethernet, Wireless, VPN, etc.)
steps.expect: Condition matches the NAS-Port-Type sent by the NAS device

steps.action: Add or correct Windows Group condition to include the authenticating user's group membership
steps.expect: User's group membership matches the policy condition

steps.action: Reorder Network Policies so that more specific policies are evaluated before generic ones
steps.expect: First matching policy wins — ensure correct policy applies

steps.action: Create a catch-all policy with minimal conditions if appropriate for the environment
steps.expect: Requests that don't match specific policies fall through to catch-all policy

phases.name: Confirm
phases.description: Verify Network Policy matching succeeds after condition fixes.

steps.action: Get-WinEvent -LogName Security -FilterXPath "*[System[(EventID=6272)]]" | Select -First 3 | Format-List TimeCreated,Message
steps.expect: Event 6272 = authentication succeeded — policy matched

steps.action: Review NPS IAS log for policy name that matched
steps.expect: Log shows which Network Policy granted access

steps.action: Test authentication from affected client or NAS
steps.expect: Authentication succeeds with correct policy applied

vlan_assignment_failure.title: VLAN assignment not working via RADIUS
vlan_assignment_failure.description: This playbook addresses issues where VLAN assignments configured in NPS Network Policies are not being applied by the NAS device. Common causes include incorrect RADIUS attribute configuration (Tunnel-Pvt-Group-ID attribute 81), NAS device not configured to use RADIUS VLAN attributes, incorrect VLAN IDs, and switch configuration issues. VLAN assignment is used in 802.1X deployments to dynamically assign network segments based on user identity or device type. The playbook verifies NPS attribute configuration and NAS device settings.

phases.name: Verify
phases.description: Verify NPS Network Policy has correct VLAN attributes configured.

steps.action: netsh nps show np
steps.expect: Network Policy includes Tunnel-Pvt-Group-ID (attribute 81) or other VLAN-related attributes

steps.action: Review NPS console: Network Policy > Settings > RADIUS Attributes
steps.expect: VLAN ID is correctly configured in standard or vendor-specific attributes

steps.action: Check NAS device configuration for RADIUS VLAN assignment
steps.expect: NAS is configured to use RADIUS attributes for VLAN assignment

phases.name: Isolate
phases.description: Isolate whether the issue is with NPS attribute configuration or NAS device configuration.

steps.action: Review NPS IAS log for attributes sent in Access-Accept packet
steps.expect: Log shows Tunnel-Pvt-Group-ID and other VLAN attributes in the response

steps.action: Capture RADIUS packet trace on NPS or NAS
steps.expect: Access-Accept packet contains VLAN attributes with correct values

steps.action: Check switch logs for VLAN assignment errors
steps.expect: Switch logs show whether VLAN assignment was attempted and any errors

steps.action: Verify VLAN ID exists on the switch and is configured on the correct ports
steps.expect: VLAN ID is valid and configured on the switch

phases.name: Fix
phases.description: Fix VLAN assignment by correcting NPS attributes or NAS device configuration.

steps.action: Configure correct Tunnel-Pvt-Group-ID attribute in NPS Network Policy
steps.expect: Attribute value matches the desired VLAN ID

steps.action: Configure NAS device to use RADIUS vendor-specific attributes if required for the specific switch vendor
steps.expect: NAS interprets vendor-specific VLAN attributes correctly

steps.action: Enable RADIUS-assigned VLAN on switch ports
steps.expect: Switch ports accept VLAN assignments from RADIUS

steps.action: Verify VLAN exists and is active on the switch
steps.expect: VLAN is configured and operational on the switch

phases.name: Confirm
phases.description: Verify VLAN assignment works correctly after configuration fixes.

steps.action: Test authentication and verify client is placed in correct VLAN
steps.expect: Client device is assigned to the correct VLAN based on policy

steps.action: Check client IP address and verify it matches the VLAN subnet
steps.expect: Client receives IP address from the correct VLAN subnet

steps.action: Review switch port status to confirm VLAN assignment
steps.expect: Switch port shows the assigned VLAN for the authenticated client
